title: Diversity in Coded TE-QKD Channels: Achieving Infinite Diversity out of Finite System Resources
authors: Shaikha S. Al-Qahtani, Siyao Li, Joseph J. Boutros
abstract: We establish conditions and give proofs on how an error-correcting code can attain infinite diversity in a time-entanglement quantum key distribution (TE-QKD) reconciliation. The shocking result, never encountered in the literature on coding and communication theory, is that a decoder exhibits an infinite diversity order while the channel has finite diversity and the code has a relatively short finite length.   This paper studies the diversity order of coded TE-QKD reconciliation, defined by the asymptotic slope of the error probability at high signal-to-noise ratio. For bounded-distance algebraic decoding, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of the number of photons per codeword and the decoding radius.   For soft-decision decoding, we introduce the maximal finite diversity (MFD) property and prove that infinite diversity is achieved if and only if the code is MFD deficient. The infinite diversity in TE-QKD has no counterpart in classical fading channels, where decoding can only multiply a finite diversity order by a finite factor.   Examples of short codes based on Golay, Reed-Solomon, Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH), and Reed-Muller codes validate the analysis and illustrate how the TE-QKD system parameters and the relatively short code parameters affect the achievable diversity for both hard and soft information reconciliation.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes error correction in Time-Entanglement Quantum Key Distribution (TE-QKD) to determine conditions for high reliability. It establishes that by using specific error-correcting codes and soft decoding techniques, the system can achieve 'infinite diversity' despite having a physically finite channel diversity. This result is significant because it demonstrates a coding advantage unmatched in classical communication theory.
main_problem: The core problem is establishing the conditions under which an error-correcting code can achieve infinite diversity order in Time-Entanglement Quantum Key Distribution (TE-QKD) reconciliation.
main_result: The paper proves that for soft-decision decoding, infinite diversity is achieved if and only if the underlying code possesses the Maximal Finite Diversity (MFD) deficient property. This behavior is unique compared to classical fading channels.
method: The analysis involves deriving necessary and sufficient conditions using asymptotic limits of error probabilities ($P_e$) with respect to the Signal-to-Noise Ratio ($\gamma$), comparing algebraic vs. soft decoding approaches.
model_or_system: The system is TE-QKD, where raw key bits are encoded across time bins affected by Gaussian noise modeling detector timing jitter. The analysis uses coded error-correcting codes (e.g., Golay, BCH) to process this noisy quantum channel output.
key_observables: Diversity Order ($d$), Reconciliation Error Probability ($P_e(\gamma)$), and the Maximal Finite Diversity (MFD) property.
important_parameters: Signal-to-Noise Ratio ($\gamma$), number of photons per codeword, and the decoding radius.
main_assumptions: The model assumes independent photon-pair realizations and memoryless detector jitters across channel uses. The analysis focuses on high SNR asymptotic behavior.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the frame structure in TE-QKD, showing the physical positions of photons before and after being corrupted by detection jitter noise.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the diversity order based on error probability decay. It then analyzes two decoding regimes: bounded-distance algebraic decoding (deriving necessary/sufficient conditions) and soft-decision decoding (introducing and utilizing the MFD property).
why_interesting: It provides a novel theoretical result showing how coding theory can fundamentally alter the asymptotic performance limits of quantum communication channels, achieving an infinite diversity gain unattainable in classical fading models.
